subject: Cloud Computing
title: What Is Edge Computing?
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on What Is Edge Computing?.

hook.text: The cloud is moving closer to you. Edge computing puts processing power near the devices that need it most.

buildup.text: Sending data to a distant data center adds latency. For self-driving cars or AR glasses, milliseconds matter.

discovery.text: Edge nodes process data locally — at cell towers, factories, or retail stores — and sync results with the cloud later.

twist.text: Edge computing doesn't replace the cloud. It extends it. The cloud becomes a hierarchy: edge, region, and central.

climax.text: By 2025, Gartner predicts 75% of enterprise data will be processed outside traditional data centers. The edge is here.

punchline.text: The cloud is moving to your doorstep. Closer means faster.

quiz.question: Why is edge computing important for applications like self-driving cars?
options: It processes data locally, reducing the latency that distant data centers introduce
Self-driving cars have no internet connection at all
Edge computing is cheaper than cloud computing for all use cases

details.summary: Edge computing processes data near its source rather than sending everything to distant cloud data centers. By placing compute resources at cell towers, retail stores, and factories, edge computing delivers ultra-low latency for applications that cannot tolerate network delays.
details.whyItMatters: Edge computing extends cloud capabilities to places where centralized computing is too slow. It enables real-time applications like autonomous vehicles and industrial automation that need sub-millisecond response times.
takeaways: Edge computing processes data near where it is generated
It reduces latency from hundreds of milliseconds to single digits
Applications like autonomous vehicles depend on edge processing

faq.question: How does edge computing differ from cloud computing?
faq.answer: Cloud computing centralizes processing in large data centers. Edge computing distributes processing to smaller locations near data sources. Most architectures use both: edge handles latency-sensitive processing while cloud handles heavy computation, storage, and analytics.

faq.question: Where are edge computing resources located?
faq.answer: Edge locations include cell tower bases, retail stores, factory floors, hospital equipment rooms, and small regional facilities. Cloud providers also offer edge zones in major cities, placing their infrastructure closer to users than traditional cloud regions.
